params.body:
One list had blue column headers where every other one has quiet grey ones. It turned out to be a
single screen and a single rule.

The contracts list carried `<thead class="orange">`, and this sat in `app.scss`:

```scss
table thead.orange {
    tr th, tr td { color: $bootstrap-primary-color; }
}
```

`$bootstrap-primary-color` is `#009DE0` — **a blue**. The bought theme calls its accent "orange" and
somebody set it to the client's blue years ago, so a class named after one colour paints another.
Nothing in the blade told you that; you had to follow the name into the sass to find out it lies.

It was the only view using the class and the only rule using it. Both are gone, and the list now
looks like its neighbours: `.ui-list thead th`, grey, 12.5px, one line underneath. Which also
answers the second half of the question — yes, blue headers are too much: the colour is the accent
for things you can act on, and a column name is not one of those.

`TableHeadersTest` keeps it that way. A `thead` may carry behaviour (`sticky-top` is the one that
exists) and never paint. A list that needs its own look says so on the table, in `refresh.css`,
where the whole family can be read in one place instead of hiding in a sass partial.

params.title: One list shouted its column headers in blue
